All sections (including stub generator)
* "Led" should be spelled as "lead".

Goal
* Perhaps simplify "steps, represented by" to "steps of"?

* Please change 1), 2) and 3) to Lines 1, 2 and 3, or specify that 1), 2) and 3) are line numbers.

Input
* Please mention that the push power is an integer.

Output
* Please add "<<3 lines:>>" at the beginning, and remove the second sentence.

Constraints
* Please mention the range of values of push power.

Constraints / Cases
* Please either add a new pair of cases where the final length of [[led]] is 0, or add a constraint stating that such a scenario won't appear in the cases.

Cases
* The test and the validator aren't closely aligned in the last two pairs of cases.

  - Consider splitting Pair 4 into three pairs of cases:
  
   (a) a PUSH command whose push power is smaller than the lead's current length,
   
   (b) the opposite scenario,

   (c) PUSH when the length of the lead is 0.

  - [[width]] = 3 appears in a test only but not a validator. Please make sure to cover the same scenario in a validator.

  - For the original Pair 5, please revise both cases to include all three commands and PUSH scenarios (a) and (b), with [[n]] close or equal to its upper bound of 15.

Thanks.

Thanks for your review @5DN1L! I have gotten to work on your suggestions, but I want to ask about calling [[push power]] an integer. When you get the PUSH command, it comes in a pair with the push power, but it is all just one string. ex. "PUSH 8". So calling that an integer might be confusing since I don't know how to make the stub-generator automatically turn push-power into an integer.

You can't. You can keep push power in the current form (i.e. format it in <<bold>> instead of treating it as a [[variable]]), but just mention that it is an integer in the description. I also think that's necessary instead of confusing. Without the restriction, one might think push power can be a float, for example.
Alright; I fixed all of your suggestions! If it looks good to you, then I'll set the status to Ready.

I'll review it in more detail a bit later, as I'm having dinner at the moment, but some quick points first:

Input
* led => lead

Output
* Checklist… 😉

Constraints
* Please remove the last constraint. It's a rule (not a constraint) already stated at the end of the Goal section, so there's no need to repeat it here. In any case, the lead length must never be less than 0 at any stage, not only in the final state.

Thanks.
Thanks @5DN1L! I fixed the remaining led typos to lead, removed my checklist, and removed the last constraint. I'll wait for your detailed review; enjoy dinner!

Thanks @VINCE_MX. I've had a chance to take a closer look now. A few more comments below:

Input
* Line 1, Line 2: Please change "led" to "lead".

Cases
* Pushing On Air (test) and VD #6: Please remove the CLOSE command. Since CLOSE cancels the effects of all preceding commands, including it prevents proper testing of the scenario where PUSH is executed when the lead length is 0.
👍 I don't have further comments at the moment. 😊
